title: Command to verify quadlet files
body:
### Feature request description

I'm running a lot of quadlets on my homelab and recently discovered one of them wasn't being run. I could see it picked up in `podman quadlet list` but had a status of `Not loaded`. Checking the file itself I didn't see anything wrong with it and was clueless until I found `/usr/lib/systemd/system-generators/podman-system-generator` which told me what the error was - I had renamed a volume a while back and not updated it here.

It isn't obvious why a quadlet isn't loaded nor is it easy to know if it is an issue in the file or somewhere else using the commands available through `podman`

### Suggest potential solution

Expose a new command `podman quadlet verify` or `podman quadlet info <name>`

### Have you considered any alternatives?

Can run `/usr/lib/systemd/system-generators/podman-system-generator --dryrun` to get information

### Additional context

_No response_

comments.body:
Hi @Venefilyn , I’m interested in working on this issue and exploring a possible implementation of `podman quadlet verify`.

I’m currently looking into how Quadlet discovery/loading and `podman-system-generator` work, and I’d like to understand the expected behavior before starting the implementation.

Would you be able to share an example of the Quadlet configuration that resulted in `Not loaded`, along with the kind of diagnostic output you would ideally expect from `podman quadlet verify`?

I’d be happy to investigate this and work toward a PR.
I think it is a good idea. Feel free to start designing the solution. @Ramya0405 (Suggest to create desing doc before you start implementing anything.)
